newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Orange, CAIB bid for Austria GSM licence.
newsitem.headline: Orange, CAIB bid for Austria GSM licence.

text.p: Britain's Orange Plc and Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CAIB) entered the bidding for Austria's third mobile telephone licence ahead of Wednesday's deadline, Creditanstalt said.

The joint bid, in which Creditanstalt has a 51 percent stake, is up against the long standing Connect Austria consortium, which groups Austria's Radex-Heraklith, Germany's Viag, unlisted Constantia Privatbank and bank GiroCredit of Austria.
Austrian media have speculated that the government will have difficulty raising more than 1.5 billion schillings from the third auction because of setting up costs.

The nation's mobile phone network is almost entirely dominated by Mobilkom Austria, a unit of state postal and telecoms monopoly PTA. The market is due for liberalisation in 1998, one year ahead of PTA's planned privatisation.
Mobilkom is estimated to have some 650,000 mobile phone customers in Austria, a country of eight million, with about four million of them in the GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) segment.
Max.mobil's customer base is believed to be 25,000. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
